wdi.name: World Bank, World Development Indicators, last updated 2026-10-08 (49 series; every series' own metadata gives License_Type CC BY-4.0, checked 2026-10-30)

oecd.name: OECD data, credit to the OECD per dataset: Earnings (average and minimum wages), Financial market (long-term interest rates), Social Expenditure (public old-age pensions), National Accounts at a Glance (households), Regions, cities and local areas (functional urban areas: economy, population, density), Affordable Housing Database (HM1.1 housing stock, HC3.1 homelessness)
oecd.licence: OECD terms and conditions, Data: permitted for any purpose, even commercial, with credit (https://www.oecd.org/en/about/terms-conditions.html)

bis.name: Bank for International Settlements, central bank policy rates (WS_CBPOL), monthly, bulk file WS_CBPOL_csv_col.zip
bis.licence: BIS terms of permitted use of statistics: unrestricted with the BIS cited, not misleading, and no additional charge to users of a commercial product (https://data.bis.org/help/legal)

wup.name: United Nations, DESA, Population Division, World Urbanization Prospects 2025 (the 22nd revision), cities of 50,000 people or more, Degree of Urbanization

eia.name: US Energy Information Administration, International Energy Statistics (INTL bulk file, series updated 2026-10-16)
eia.licence: public domain (a US government work); source: U.S. Energy Information Administration

world-1.name: The game's nations' world file, world-1.bin (batch WN0): its 2025 path figures, made from the World Bank's WDI (CC BY 4.0), the UN's World Population Prospects 2024 (CC BY 3.0 IGO), the Penn World Table 11.0 (CC BY 4.0) and the Maddison Project Database 2023 (CC BY 4.0)
world-1.licence: CC BY 4.0 and CC BY 3.0 IGO, its sources' own

bls.name: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, CPI-U, US city average, all items (CUUR0000SA0), annual averages

rules.ppp-market: A nation with no published figure at purchasing power parity takes its figure at market exchange rates, the same value and year, as the best estimate there is.
rules.world-1: A nation the World Bank has no figure for in 2015-2025 takes the game's own estimate for 2025, made for the nations' world file from the Penn World Table, the Maddison Project and the UN's population estimates.
rules.share-people: A city region the OECD publishes no share of its nation's output for takes its share of the nation's people as its share of the output.
rules.region-output: A city region's GDP is its share of its nation's output times the nation's figure; where the share and the nation's figure are not of one year, or the share is itself an estimate, the result is the game's estimate, not a published figure.

definitions.oecd: The OECD's functional urban area: a city and its commuting zone.
definitions.wup: The UN's urban centre: contiguous 1 km² cells of at least 1,500 people a km², 50,000 people in all (World Urbanization Prospects 2025).

measures.name: GDP
measures.note: current US$; also kept at constant 2015 US$ (NY.GDP.MKTP.KD) and at PPP, current international $ (NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.CD)

measures.name: GDP per person
measures.note: current US$; also at constant 2015 US$ (NY.GDP.PCAP.KD) and at PPP (NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.CD)

measures.name: real growth
measures.note: GDP at constant prices, the year over the year before. A city region's is its functional urban area's GDP (OECD, USD_PPP) in its latest year over the year before; the OECD's metadata does not say the series is at constant prices, but the US areas' implied national total falls 2.2% in 2020 and rises 5.8% in 2021, tracking the WDI's real growth (-2.1, 6.2) and not the nominal (about -0.9, +10.7)

measures.name: 10-year growth
measures.note: GDP at constant 2015 US$, compound yearly growth over the ten years to the figure's year

measures.name: household spending per person
measures.note: households' final consumption, current US$, over the people

measures.name: trade balance
measures.note: exports less imports of goods and services

measures.name: taking part in work
measures.note: labour force participation rate, ILO modelled estimate

measures.name: average wage
measures.note: average annual wage, current prices, at the year's exchange rate

measures.name: minimum wage
measures.note: statutory minimum wage a year, current prices, at the year's exchange rate. Bulgaria's, which the OECD gives in euros, is converted to levs at the peg first

measures.name: minimum against average wage
measures.note: the minimum wage over the mean wage of full-time workers

measures.name: inflation
measures.note: consumer prices, the year's average over the year before

measures.name: policy rate
measures.source: bis:WS_CBPOL_csv_col.zip|FREQ=M,nation=REF_AREA(ISO2),time=columns 2025-12 back to 2025-01 (the last one not empty),value=that cell
measures.note: the central bank's policy rate at the year's end. The 20 euro-area members, whose own series ended before the euro, take the euro area's rate (BIS REF_AREA=XM), mark 3

measures.name: 10-year yield
measures.note: long-term government bond yield, the year's average

measures.name: real interest rate
measures.note: lending rate less the GDP deflator's inflation

measures.name: currency against parity
measures.note: the market rate over the PPP rate, both local money a US$: above 1, the money buys more at home than its market rate says. Bulgaria's PPP factor, which the WDI gives in euros, is converted to levs at the peg first

measures.name: price level against the US
measures.note: the PPP conversion factor over the market rate (the US is 1). Bulgaria's PPP factor, which the WDI gives in euros, is converted to levs at the peg first

measures.name: debt in foreign money
measures.source: none:no open source publishes the currency share of public debt for most nations (the IMF's terms do not allow it)

measures.name: budget balance
measures.note: central government net lending (+) or borrowing (-)

measures.name: interest
measures.note: central government interest payments over revenue

measures.name: city fund
measures.source: none:no source whose terms let a game ship them publishes sovereign funds' assets

measures.name: credit rating
measures.source: none:the rating agencies' terms do not let a game ship their ratings

measures.name: pensions
measures.note: public spending on old-age and survivors' pensions

measures.name: bank capital ratio
measures.note: bank capital and reserves over total assets

measures.name: credit to firms and households
measures.note: domestic credit to the private sector

measures.name: stock market
measures.note: market capitalisation of listed domestic companies

measures.name: household debt
measures.note: households' debt over their net disposable income

measures.name: net migration
measures.note: arrivals less departures in the year

measures.name: people per household
measures.source: none:no source the study names publishes it for most nations

measures.name: rent
measures.source: none:no comparable published figure across nations (D10's rule)

measures.name: homes per 1,000
measures.source: oecd:AHD_HM1-1-Housing-stock-and-construction.xlsx|sheet=HM1.1.A1,nation=col A (the country name),value=col J else col I,time=col M else col L
measures.note: the housing stock (OECD Affordable Housing Database). The UK is England

measures.name: without a home per 10,000
measures.source: oecd:AHD_HC3-1-Population-experiencing-homelessness.xlsx|sheet=Table_HC3.1.A1,nation=col A (the country name),value=col B (a fraction of the people; a text cell is read as a percent and NA skipped),time=col J (its first four digits),mul=10000
measures.note: the homeless counted (OECD Affordable Housing Database). The counts differ by nation (a point in time or a flow, children in or out); Belgium and the UK, which the workbook splits by region, are left out

measures.name: households sharing
measures.source: none:no comparable published figure across nations

measures.name: home price to income
measures.source: none:the OECD's price-to-income series is an index, not a level that ranks

measures.name: prisoners
measures.source: none:UNODC allows personal non-commercial use only on its current terms page (older dataUNODC terms allowed free reuse if cited); Jerus to decide, see MEASURES-SOURCES.txt

measures.name: police
measures.source: none:UNODC allows personal non-commercial use only on its current terms page (older dataUNODC terms allowed free reuse if cited); Jerus to decide, see MEASURES-SOURCES.txt

measures.name: water per person
measures.note: annual freshwater withdrawals over the people

measures.name: cars per 1,000
measures.source: none:no source the study names publishes it (the WDI's series ended; OICA's terms)

measures.name: commutes by transit
measures.source: none:no comparable published figure across nations or cities

measures.name: oil produced
measures.source: eia:INTL.zip|file=INTL.txt (one JSON series a line),series_id=INTL.57-1-<ISO3>-TBPD.A,time=data[n][0],value=data[n][1] (thousand barrels a day)
